bill.title: Improving Access to Transfusion Care for Hospice Patients Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bill.officialSummary: Improving Access to Transfusion Care for Hospice Patients Act of 2026 This bill requires the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) to test a model under which blood transfusions furnished to an individual receiving hospice care are paid separately from the hospice all-inclusive per diem payment under Medicare. The CMMI must evaluate the model by comparing patients participating in the model with those outside of the model in relation to specified metrics, such as hospital utilization and days of hospice care before the end of life.

classification.plainSummary: This bill directs Medicare to test a new payment model for hospice patients who need blood transfusions. Currently, hospice care is paid through a single daily rate that covers all services. The bill would allow blood transfusions to be billed separately, then compare patients in the pilot program to those outside it on measures like hospital use and length of hospice enrollment.

industries.rationale: Hospice providers would receive separate payment for transfusions rather than covering them under the per-diem rate, directly affecting their revenue structure.
Medicare payment models for hospice services would change, affecting how the program reimburses for transfusion care.
Blood product suppliers and medical device companies providing transfusion equipment would see changes in how their products are paid for in hospice settings.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would require the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a model under which blood transfusions furnished to an individual receiving hospice care are paid separately from the hospice all-inclusive per diem payment under Medicare.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who sees a doctor or pays for care.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in getting care, and paying for it. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
